findings.evidence: Line 299-300 `def IsEffective : Prop := hs.F 0 = ⊤ ∧ hs.F (n + 1) = ⊥`; no other occurrence of `Hodge.IsEffective` in the repo. Roadmap README L0 names it as the hypothesis under which the weight-1 identifications hold, so its content matters downstream.
findings.fix: Add the characterization (`hs.IsEffective → ∀ p, p < 0 ∨ n < p → hs.piece ω p = ⊥`, ideally as an iff) and a witness, e.g. `(tate 0).IsEffective` — for `m = 0` the conditions read `0 ≤ 0` and `¬(1 ≤ 0)`, both discharged by the same `ite_eq_left`/`ite_eq_right` pattern already used in `tate`.
findings.issue: `IsEffective` is a new Prop-valued definition with no consuming theorem and no witness anywhere in the PR or on main (grep for `IsEffective` in `code/` finds only this definition and the module docstring; the other hits are `WeilDivisor`/`Algebra.IsEffective`, unrelated). Its docstring and the module docstring at line 32 claim it means "the Hodge numbers are supported in [0, n]", but nothing links `F 0 = ⊤ ∧ F (n+1) = ⊥` to `piece ω p = ⊥` for `p < 0` or `p > n`, so the claim is unverified.

findings.evidence: Line 434 `tate` and line 480 `tate_piece_apply` both use `latticeConjugation (complexificationMap_isBaseChange (V := ℤ))`, never `concreteConjugation`; `latticeConj_unique` (line 241) already supplies exactly the identification and is itself otherwise unused.
findings.fix: Add `concreteLatticeConj = latticeConj (complexificationMap_isBaseChange (V := V))` (hence `concreteConjugation V = latticeConjugation _`), proved in one line by `latticeConj_unique` — the hypothesis `concreteLatticeConj (complexificationMap v) = complexificationMap v` is `concreteLatticeConj_tmul 1 v` plus `map_one`. `tate` can then discharge its `h_top_map` steps through the concrete map.
findings.issue: `concreteConjugation` / `concreteLatticeConj` are advertised (docstrings lines 22-23, 94-95) as the canonical conjugation on `ℂ ⊗[ℤ] V`, but nothing in the PR proves they agree with `latticeConjugation (complexificationMap_isBaseChange)`, which is what `HodgeStructure`, `tate`, and `tate_piece_apply` actually use. `concreteConjugation` has no consumer at all (grep: only its own definition site), so the two canonical conjugations on the same space are left unrelated and a user reasoning with `concreteLatticeConj` can apply no Hodge result.

summary: The Hodge decomposition, the (p,q) conjugation symmetry, and the Tate witness are mathematically faithful and I could not break them. Two unfalsifiable declarations remain: `IsEffective` has no consumer, no witness, and its docstring claim is unproved; and the concrete conjugation is never identified with the abstract one actually used.
